CFML Language Reference: Functions

DateDiff

Counts how many complete units of a datepart lie between two dates. The result is positive if the second date is later than the first, negative if it is earlier.

Category

Date and time functions

Syntax

DateDiff(datepart, date1, date2)

Parameters

datepart
The unit to count, one of: yyyy years, q quarters, m months, y days, d days, w days, ww weeks, h hours, n minutes, s seconds.
date1
The starting date/time value, or a string that can be converted to one.
date2
The ending date/time value, or a string that can be converted to one.

Returns

A whole number: date2 minus date1, in the units asked for. Partial units are dropped (rounded toward zero).

Usage

Years, quarters and months count completed calendar months: from December 31, 1999 to January 1, 2000 is 1 day but 0 years, even though the year number changed. To see whether two dates fall in different years, compare Year() values instead.

In KoldFusion y, d and w all count days, and ww counts whole weeks. Note the argument order: the earlier date normally comes first.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Start = CreateDateTime(1999, 1, 1, 9, 0, 0)>
<CFSET Y2K = CreateDateTime(2000, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)>
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>From #DateFormat(Start, "mmm d, yyyy")# #TimeFormat(Start, "h:mm tt")#
to the year 2000:</P>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Datepart</TH><TH>DateDiff</TH></TR>
<CFLOOP INDEX="Part" LIST="yyyy,q,m,ww,d,h">
<TR><TD>#Part#</TD><TD ALIGN="RIGHT">#DateDiff(Part, Start, Y2K)#</TD></TR>
</CFLOOP>
</TABLE>
<P>Dec 31, 1999 to Jan 1, 2000: #DateDiff("d", "12/31/1999", "1/1/2000")# day,
#DateDiff("yyyy", "12/31/1999", "1/1/2000")# years.</P>
</CFOUTPUT>

DateAdd, DatePart, DateCompare, CreateTimeSpan
